Imbibe

im-BYB · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To imbibe to drink, absorb, or assimilate.

The young apprentice seemed to imbibe every piece of advice the master craftsman offered.

Worked Example

The eager exchange student seemed to imbibe the local traditions within just a few weeks.

Imbibe is often used figuratively for absorbing ideas, culture, or advice, just as it is used literally for drinking.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — sample → wolf down → imbibe

sample vs. imbibe

sample vs. imbibe: Sampling something is trying a little of it; imbibing it means taking it in fully.

wolf down vs. imbibe

wolf down vs. imbibe: To wolf something down is to take it in completely and eagerly, a step beyond simply imbibing it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: into (variant of in-) (Latin)

root — bibe

root — bibe: to drink (Latin (bibere))

Put it together

Put it together: im- ("into") + bibe ("to drink") = to take in by drinking.

Use the root in a new word: beverage

Use the root in a new word: beverage: That same "bibere" root traveled through Old French to give us the everyday word "beverage."
